items.q: What is the Greek Golden Visa?
items.a: A five-year residence permit for non-EU nationals who invest in Greek real estate. It is renewable every five years for as long as you keep the property, and it gives visa-free travel within the Schengen Area for up to 90 days in any 180.

items.q: Do I have to live in Greece to keep it?
items.a: No. There is no minimum stay. You can spend as much or as little of the year in Greece as you like and the permit stays valid.

items.q: Does the Golden Visa lead to EU citizenship?
items.a: Not automatically. The permit grants long-term residence. Citizenship is a separate naturalisation process with its own requirements, including years of actual residence, language and civic knowledge.

items.q: Can I work in Greece with a Golden Visa?
items.a: The permit does not include the right to be employed in Greece, but you can invest, own companies, and act as a shareholder or board member.

Since 2024 it depends on the location: €800,000 in Attica (all of Athens, including Glyfada and Piraeus), the Thessaloniki regional unit, Mykonos, Santorini and islands with more than 3,100 residents, and €400,000 everywhere else, in both cases for one residential property of at least 120 m². A €250,000 threshold applies anywhere in Greece to a building converted from commercial to residential use (the conversion must be completed before you apply) and to a listed building that is restored (by the first renewal). Our advisors confirm which route applies to each Netherfield property before you reserve.

items.q: Can I combine several properties to reach the threshold?
items.a: For the €400,000 and €800,000 routes the investment has to be a single property of at least 120 m². Additional homes can of course be bought alongside it.

items.q: Can I rent the property out?
items.a: Yes, on long-term leases. Golden Visa properties may not be used for short-term holiday rentals such as Airbnb; breaking this rule can cost the permit and a €50,000 fine. Netherfield's rental team can find and manage long-term tenants for you.
Netherfield's portfolio has averaged a 6% gross annual rental yield. Returns vary by property, furnishing and lease, and are never guaranteed; we share the figures behind each estimate.

items.q: Who can be included in the application?
items.a: Your spouse or registered partner, your unmarried children under 21, and the parents of both spouses, all under the one investment.

items.q: What happens when the permit is renewed?
items.a: Every five years the permit is renewed for the whole family, as long as you still own the qualifying property.

items.q: How long does the process take?
items.a: It depends on the property and the paperwork. Once due diligence is complete, buying usually takes a few weeks; the residence permit follows after your biometrics appointment, typically within several months. We give you a realistic timeline in your first consultation.

items.q: What costs come on top of the purchase price?
items.a: Expect property transfer tax (3.09% on resale homes; new builds may be subject to VAT instead), notary, land registry and legal fees, and the permit application fees. Your advisor prepares a full cost breakdown before you commit.

items.q: Do I need to be in Greece to buy?
items.a: Only briefly. With a power of attorney our legal partners can handle most steps for you; you visit once to give your biometrics for the permit.
